default_action.when: MALLOC_ARENA_MAX is absent and no colon-delimited GLIBC_TUNABLES glibc.malloc.arena_max= entry is present

caller_override.MALLOC_ARENA_MAX: Any present value, including empty or invalid, is preserved; no coercion or validation is performed.
caller_override.GLIBC_TUNABLES: An exact glibc.malloc.arena_max= entry suppresses injection, including an empty value. All tunables are passed through unchanged.
caller_override.both_present: Preserve both; GNU libc resolves precedence. No promise that MALLOC_ARENA_MAX is the effective control.
caller_override.unrelated_tunables: Preserve and still inject the selected MALLOC_ARENA_MAX default.
caller_override.scope: Environment of this exec only, naturally inherited by subprocesses that do not replace or remove it. No global or service configuration.

launch.argv: absolute executable path followed by unchanged runtime arguments
launch.stdout: no wrapper output; owned by child protocol
launch.exec: replace shell with executable, retain PID, normal exit/signal semantics
launch.binary_hashing: not performed per invocation; qualify and bind the artifact before launch
launch.platform_check: Linux and GNU libc; no assertion that other Linux/glibc hardware is qualified

formal_comparison.baseline: driver constructs a clean allocator environment: no MALLOC_* or GLIBC_TUNABLES
formal_comparison.candidate: same qualified R14 executable; driver explicitly supplies MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1
formal_comparison.verification: driver records post-exec /proc/PID/environ for each long-lived controller and restart, plus binary/configuration fingerprints
formal_comparison.purpose: separate allocator setting effect from caller environment; ordinary wrapper preserves explicit caller controls

limitations: Causal diagnostics are not throughput benchmarks; background archive/audit I/O overlapped.
One arena may increase allocator lock contention in other workloads; native C8 and recovery remain required formal gates.
This profile changes memory allocation policy for the process; it does not limit Tokio thread count.
Publication concurrency remains 8 and physical cancellation preparation remains 2 in the unchanged R14 source.
